caption: The drawing features a rectangular textile item, depicted in grayscale, with intricate knitted or crocheted patterns. The composition displays the textile laid flat, seen from a top-down perspective. At the center, there are four large squares, each containing a symmetrical design that resembles a four-petaled flower or leaf motif, created by the use of denser yarn work in the petals/leaves and more open, mesh-like stitches between them. These four squares are aligned in a 2x2 grid, with diagonal lines radiating from the corners of each square, giving a sense of geometric symmetry. Surrounding the central grid is a series of borders with varying patterns; the first border consists of parallel openwork stripes, the next features a repeating set of raised oval or pod shapes, and the outermost edge has a scalloped lace border. The entire textile is rendered with fine shading and texture to illustrate the details of the stitching and fabric. The background is plain, with no additional objects present, and the artist's signature “Erwin Schwabe” appears in the lower right corner.
title: Cotton Thread Scarf
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
